findings.description: __aexit__ discards the actual exception arguments and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so exceptions raised inside the async with block are never recorded on the retry state.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an exception is raised inside `async with AttemptManager(...)`. The sync __exit__ receives exc_type/exc_value and calls set_exception to record the failure so the retry loop can decide whether to retry. Because __aexit__ passes None, the exception is treated as success: set_result(None) is called and the exception is suppressed, so the attempt is reported as successful and the error is silently swallowed rather than retried.
